units.title: Decide the customer before the experience

claim.text: The source says that before deciding what the experience should be, you must first decide who your customer is and what you do for them.
claim.quote: before deciding this whole thing with experience what the experience should be you first have to decide who is your customer and what do you do for them

action.text: Decide who your customer is and what you do for them before defining the desired experience.
action.quote: before deciding this whole thing with experience what the experience should be you first have to decide who is your customer and what do you do for them

unknowns: No method for identifying the customer or what you do for them is stated.

units.title: Know customers in depth

claim.text: The source asks whether you know customers in more depth, including key motivators, attitudes, values in business relationships, personal purposes, and how your organization makes them feel.
claim.quote: know them in more depth and that means do you know their key motivators not just with your product or your service but the key motivators for them do you know their attitudes towards your products and services do you know what they value in a relationship in business do you know what personal purposes they have and is your organization set up to really understand the way that you are making your customers feel

action.text: Know customers in more depth across key motivators, attitudes, values, personal purposes, and customer feelings.
action.quote: know them in more depth and that means do you know their key motivators not just with your product or your service but the key motivators for them do you know their attitudes towards your products and services do you know what they value in a relationship in business do you know what personal purposes they have and is your organization set up to really understand the way that you are making your customers feel

unknowns: No method or depth criteria for assessing customers is stated.

units.title: Link customer experience to business purpose

claim.text: The source says every organization exists for a purpose, and that purpose is not to make money; the rest have a purpose to bring something to life.
claim.quote: every organization exists for a purpose and no it is not to make money there is only one organization that does that and that is the one that prints money the rest have a purpose to bring something to life

unknowns: The source does not define how to articulate an organization's purpose.

units.title: Create a customer strategy as an umbrella

claim.text: The source recommends a customer strategy that acts as an umbrella over the whole organization, defining what customers should feel and the customer principles, and translating them into practice.
claim.quote: a customer strategy it's like this umbrella over the whole organization that everything you do is towards what you want your customers to really feel and do a customer strategy includes things like what our customer strategy is I mean the CX the experience what we want our customers to feel what are the customers principles we live by and what does that translate to into practice

action.text: Define a customer strategy covering desired customer feelings, customer principles, and their practical translation.
action.quote: a customer strategy it's like this umbrella over the whole organization that everything you do is towards what you want your customers to really feel and do a customer strategy includes things like what our customer strategy is I mean the CX the experience what we want our customers to feel what are the customers principles we live by and what does that translate to into practice

unknowns: Workshop tools and methodologies for creating the customer strategy are not provided in the passage.

units.title: Design experiences; they do not happen by chance

claim.text: The source warns that customer experience left to chance will not happen by itself; experiences happen by designing them.
claim.quote: they don't just happen by chance they happen by designing the experiences

args.text: Customer experience is left to chance if not controlled.
args.quote: experience is something that would just happen and be left to chance

unknowns: No specific design method is given in this passage.

units.title: Steve Jobs: start with customer experience

claim.text: The source gives Steve Jobs as an example: when he took over Apple in 1997, he said you have to start with the customer experience and work backwards to the technology, not the other way around.
claim.quote: you have to start with the customer experience and work your way backwards to the technology and not the other way around

unknowns: The source does not give a current primary-source citation for the Jobs quote.

units.title: Assess business process capability for the customer journey

claim.text: The source asks how capable your business processes currently are in delivering your customer journey.
claim.quote: how capable are your business processes right now in delivering your customer journey

action.text: Assess how capable your business processes are to deliver your customer journey.
action.quote: how capable are your business processes right now in delivering your customer journey

unknowns: No assessment method or capability criteria stated.

units.title: Decide the product or service experience and journey

claim.text: The source says you must decide what service or product experience you want to deliver and what journey brings it to life.
claim.quote: have you decided what that service or product experience it is you want to deliver and what is the journey that brings all of this to life

action.text: Decide the service or product experience to deliver and the customer journey that brings it to life.
action.quote: have you decided what that service or product experience it is you want to deliver and what is the journey that brings all of this to life

unknowns: No decision criteria or journey components are specified.

units.title: Use customer journey mapping to design and manage experience

claim.text: The source says customer journey mapping is the tool to answer what journey brings the experience to life, and the most powerful tool to design and manage the whole experience.
claim.quote: customer journey mapping is a tool to be able to answer that question and not only that it's the most powerful tool to design and manage the whole experience

action.text: Use customer journey mapping to design and manage the whole customer experience.
action.quote: customer journey mapping is a tool to be able to answer that question and not only that it's the most powerful tool to design and manage the whole experience

unknowns: The passage mentions global best practices for journey mapping but does not provide them.

units.title: Customers experience a journey, not processes

claim.text: The source states customers do not experience processes; they experience a journey, and if they cannot feel, hear, see, or touch it, it is a process not a journey.
claim.quote: customers don't experience processes they experience a journey if they cannot feel it hear it see it touch it it is not a journey it is a process

unknowns: The distinguishing criteria beyond feel/hear/see/touch are not defined.

units.title: Use a three-part CX framework: strategy, measure, people

claim.text: The source presents a simple global best-practice framework with three parts: strategy, measure, and people.
claim.quote: it has three parts you have the strategy the measure and the people

unknowns: The full framework details are not shown in the passage.

units.title: Answer the strategy questions

claim.text: Under strategy, the source asks whether you know who your customers are emotionally, what you want their experience to be, and whether everyone in the organization knows what part they play in delivering that journey.
claim.quote: do you know who your customers are now I'm talking also emotional do you know what their experience what you want their experience to be sorry there we go three does everyone in the organization know what part they play in delivering that journey

action.text: Define who customers are emotionally, the desired experience, and each person's role in delivering the journey.
action.quote: do you know who your customers are now I'm talking also emotional do you know what their experience what you want their experience to be sorry there we go three does everyone in the organization know what part they play in delivering that journey

unknowns: No method for defining emotional customer knowledge or desired experience is given.

units.title: Undefined desired experience creates clarity and measurement problems

claim.text: The source warns that if the desired customer experience has never been defined, people will not know what to do, customers are left feeling what was never defined, and the measurement part becomes challenging.
claim.quote: if the desired customer experience have never been defined how can you expect people around you to know what they are supposed to do you leave customers feeling the way that you never defined lack of clarity in this strategy part makes the second framework the second part of the framework really challenging

args.text: The desired customer experience has never been defined.
args.quote: if the desired customer experience have never been defined

units.title: Measure from the customer perspective and set improvement priorities

claim.text: Under measurement, the source asks what journey brings it all to life, whether you measure from a customer perspective rather than internal, and whether you know improvement priorities.
claim.quote: what is that journey that brings it all to life and do we measure things from a customer perspective and not our own internal do we also know what priorities we have for the improvements

action.text: Measure the customer journey from the customer perspective and identify improvement priorities.
action.quote: what is that journey that brings it all to life and do we measure things from a customer perspective and not our own internal do we also know what priorities we have for the improvements

unknowns: Types of measurements and quality tools are not specified in the passage.

units.title: Create culture and environment for customer-focused people

claim.text: Under people, the source recommends creating the right culture and environment to enable people to think and act in the customer's interests, and asks whether people know the business/CX strategy, are ambassadors, and how to enable people and processes to deliver the desired experience.
claim.quote: creating the right culture and the environment to enable people to think and act in the interests of the customer thus enabling that strategy to come alive and the questions you need to answer is do our people know the business and the customer experience strategy are people around us in ambassadors of this experience that we want to happen and how sorry I'm late in how do you enable people or your processes and so forth to deliver this desired experience

action.text: Create the right culture and environment so people know the strategy, act as ambassadors, and enable processes to deliver the desired experience.
action.quote: creating the right culture and the environment to enable people to think and act in the interests of the customer thus enabling that strategy to come alive and the questions you need to answer is do our people know the business and the customer experience strategy are people around us in ambassadors of this experience that we want to happen and how sorry I'm late in how do you enable people or your processes and so forth to deliver this desired experience

unknowns: No concrete culture-building or enablement methods are provided.

units.title: CX principles apply the same in B2B/B2G as B2C

claim.text: The source says there is no real difference for customer experience in B2B or B2G: every customer is a human being, and the principles, methodologies, and strategies are all the same; B2C is a little more advanced than B2B.
claim.quote: it doesn't matter if it's a private person it doesn't matter if it's an organ you meet a human every customer is a human being it's a person so it doesn't matter at all the principles the methodologies the strategies they're all the same

unknowns: The source does not explain how B2C being more advanced affects B2B/B2G implementation.
